summary.problem: When the floating sidebar was open, top-right toolbar buttons rendered above it because the sidebar's z-index (80) was below the top-bar layer (100). On mobile, opening the main menu while the sidebar was open would leave both visible at the same time, with the sidebar covering the menu.
summary.solution: Raise the sidebar's z-index above the top-bar buttons, and make the main menu trigger button count as a click outside the sidebar so the sidebar closes when the menu opens.

plain.title: Sidebar now stacks correctly and closes when the menu opens
plain.problem: When the sidebar was open, toolbar buttons at the top-right would float above it. On mobile, you could have both the sidebar and the main menu open together, but the sidebar would hide the menu behind it.
plain.fix: The sidebar is given a higher stacking order than the toolbar. The menu button is also treated as a click outside the sidebar, so tapping it closes the sidebar first.

steps.title: Two problems when the sidebar is open
steps.headline: Two bugs when the sidebar is open
steps.say: Top-right toolbar buttons appear above the sidebar on desktop. On mobile, opening the main menu leaves both panels visible at once with the sidebar covering the menu.
steps.narration: There are two linked problems. On desktop, when the sidebar panel is open, the toolbar buttons in the top-right corner float above it, poking through the panel. On mobile, you can have the sidebar and the main menu open at the same time, but because the sidebar sits in front, the menu is hidden behind it. Both problems come down to where the sidebar sits in the stacking order.

items.text: Top-right toolbar sits above the open sidebar in the stacking order (z-index 80 vs 100) — hard to see in a still; next step shows the layers
On mobile, opening the main menu leaves the sidebar covering it

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: The sidebar gets its stacking order from `--zIndex-ui-library`, which sits at 80 — below the top-bar layer at 100.

lines.annotation: Sidebar z-index — below the top bar at 100.
Top-bar (toolbar buttons) z-index — above the sidebar.

sources.ref: move sidebar above top layer UI so that buttons aren't above the sidebar when open

steps.title: Sidebar z-index 80 is below the top bar at 100
steps.headline: Sidebar sits below toolbar buttons in the stack
steps.say: The sidebar and the top-bar buttons share the same stacking context. At z-index 80, the sidebar loses to the toolbar at 100.
steps.narration: The sidebar and the top-bar buttons share the same CSS stacking context inside the canvas wrapper. With the sidebar variable at 80 and the top-bar variable at 100, the toolbar is always drawn on top. Raising the sidebar variable above 100 fixes the first symptom.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: The sidebar's z-index comes from a CSS variable. `Sidebar.scss` reads `--zIndex-ui-library`, and `.App-top-bar` reads `--zIndex-ui-top`. Both are inside the same `.excalidraw` stacking context.

lines.annotation: Reads the variable defined in styles.scss.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: The variable is raised from 80 to 120 and moved to after `--zIndex-ui-top` in the declaration order so the values read low-to-high.

lines.annotation: Now above ui-top (100). The sidebar paints last in the stack.

steps.title: Raising the z-index creates a problem on mobile
steps.headline: Raising the sidebar creates a new problem on mobile
steps.say: Once the sidebar is above everything, the main menu opens behind it on mobile. The sidebar has to close when the menu button is pressed, so the next steps address that.
steps.narration: Raising the sidebar above the toolbar fixes the desktop stacking — but it creates a new problem on mobile. The main menu renders inside the top-bar layer, which is now below the sidebar. If the sidebar is already open when the user taps the hamburger, the menu appears behind the sidebar. The fix must ensure that tapping the menu button closes the floating sidebar first.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: The `MainMenu` toggle sets `openMenu` but does not touch `openSidebar`. With the sidebar now above z-index 100, the menu opens hidden behind it.

code.label: main menu toggle — no sidebar close

lines.annotation: Opens or closes the menu, but does not touch openSidebar.

notes: The PR description explicitly calls this out: 'This is necessary otherwise the previous change would make the main menu below the sidebar on mobile.'

sources.ref: close sidebar when not docked when opening main menu — necessary otherwise the previous change would make the main menu below the sidebar on mobile

steps.title: Reuse the sidebar's existing outside-click close mechanism
steps.headline: Treat the menu button as an outside click
steps.say: Rather than adding sidebar-close code to every caller, the PR makes the menu button stop being an exception to the outside-click rule. The sidebar's own handler then closes it naturally.
steps.narration: The sidebar already closes on any click outside its panel. The PR takes advantage of this: instead of wiring a sidebar-close call into the main menu toggle, it simply removes the reason the menu button was exempted from the outside-click check. The sidebar's own handler does the rest.

beats.heading: The sidebar closes on outside clicks already
beats.text: The sidebar uses `useOutsideClick`. It has one explicit carve-out: clicks on `.sidebar-trigger` are ignored so the library toggle button can open and close the sidebar without double-firing.

lines.text: // If click on the library icon, do nothing so that LibraryButton

lines.annotation: The library toggle button is deliberately excluded — clicking it should not close the sidebar via this path.
Only closes when the sidebar is floating (not docked).

sources.ref: decision to reuse existing outside-click rather than add explicit sidebar close in MainMenu

steps.title: The trigger button had a global outside-click suppressor
steps.headline: The menu button carried a close-blocking marker
steps.say: The outside-click hook skips any element carrying a special data attribute. The main menu trigger button carried that attribute, so the sidebar's handler never fired when it was clicked.
steps.narration: The outside-click system has an escape hatch: a marker that makes an element invisible to those checks anywhere on the page. The main menu button carried that marker, which is why clicking it never closed the sidebar. Simply removing the marker isn't enough on its own, because the button would then immediately close the menu it just opened. A replacement is needed first.

beats.heading: Global escape hatch in the hook
beats.text: Any click landing on or inside a `[data-prevent-outside-click]` element is silently ignored by `useOutsideClick` — for every listener in the app.

lines.text: // clicking on a container that ignores outside clicks

lines.annotation: Silences the callback for all useOutsideClick users, not just the menu's own.

beats.heading: The trigger button used this attribute
beats.text: Before the PR, `DropdownMenuTrigger` placed `data-prevent-outside-click` on the button, blocking the sidebar close whenever the button was clicked.

code.label: before: trigger button blocks outside click

lines.annotation: Clicking this button never reached any outside-click callback — including the sidebar's.

steps.title: Replace the global attribute with a DOM containment check
steps.headline: Menu content checks containment instead of a marker
steps.say: A wrapper is added around both the button and the open content. When an outside-click fires, the content checks whether the click landed inside that wrapper — if so, it is really an inside click on the trigger button.
steps.narration: The replacement wraps the menu's trigger and its open content in one container. When an outside click is detected, the handler checks whether the click came from inside that container. A click on the trigger itself is ignored, so opening the menu doesn't immediately close it. Any other click — the canvas, the sidebar, anywhere else — now closes the sidebar as before.

beats.heading: Wrapping trigger and content together
beats.text: `DropdownMenu` wraps both children in a `div.dropdown-menu-container` with `display: contents` so the wrapper has no visual effect but gives the content a DOM ancestor to query.

lines.text: // remove this div from box layout

lines.annotation: display:contents makes this a DOM ancestor without affecting layout or stacking.

beats.heading: Content checks containment instead of using the attribute
beats.text: `DropdownMenuContent` receives the event and calls `onClickOutside` only when the click is outside the `.dropdown-menu-container` ancestor.

lines.text: // prevents closing if clicking on the trigger button

lines.annotation: Walks up to find the outer wrapper, then checks if the clicked element is inside it.

steps.title: The data attribute is removed from the trigger button
steps.headline: The button no longer blocks outside-click events globally
steps.say: With the containment check in place, the button's blanket suppressor can be removed. Clicks on it now reach outside-click listeners, including the sidebar's.
steps.narration: With the menu content now doing its own containment check, the button no longer needs to globally silence outside-click events. Removing the attribute is what allows the sidebar's handler to see clicks on the menu button and close the sidebar.

beats.heading: What we remove
beats.text: `data-prevent-outside-click` is dropped from the trigger button. The containment check in `DropdownMenuContent` now serves the same purpose — but only for the menu's own outside-click callback, not globally.

lines.annotation: Removed: the containment check in DropdownMenuContent now handles the trigger-button case.

skippedHunks.reason: Type-only change: callback parameter narrowed from Event to Event & { target: T } so the new containment check in DropdownMenuContent can access event.target without a cast.

openQuestions.question: Are there other places in the app that render a DropdownMenu trigger and relied on `data-prevent-outside-click` to suppress outside-click logic for panels other than the sidebar? Removing the attribute changes behavior for every useOutsideClick listener that was open at the same time.
openQuestions.why: The attribute was global across all useOutsideClick hooks. Any panel using useOutsideClick that was open while a DropdownMenu trigger was clicked would previously have been unaffected; now it will receive the outside-click.

pr.title: fix: close floating sidebar on main menu open
pr.author: dwelle
commitTitles: fix: close floating sidebar on main menu open
pr.body:
- move sidebar above top layer UI (especially top-right) so that buttons aren't above the sidebar when open
- close sidebar (when not docked) when opening main menu. This is necessary otherwise the previous change would make the main menu below the sidebar on mobile.
